title: Ind-finite etale local systems of sets and modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. A sheaf $F$ of sets is ind-finite etale if it is isomorphic to the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of a small filtered diagram of sheaves represented by finite etale $S$-schemes [def-galois-categories]. For a commutative ring $R$, an $R_S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is ind-finite etale if its underlying sheaf of sets is ind-finite etale. These module sheaves form the full subcategory of ambient module sheaves, so the arrows are all ambient module sheaf maps. For Noetherian $S$ these are the local systems of ILO XVII Definition 7.2.1 and its module variant. Neither finiteness of $R$ nor finite generation of stalks is required.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 7.2.1 and paragraph after Proposition 7.2.3, pp. 301-302.

New def node def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system: an actual filtered colimit of finite-etale representables, real content, no duplicate in DAG, live/side Lean or runs/2. Monodromy pinned by the finiteGerm field (germ at a goes to germ at g.a; every stalk element is such a germ), so the action is canonical. Cover map h pinned on all finite-cover fibres, so h = c_*. Exactness, all small colimits, kernels/cokernels, extensions, constants, descent with L not assumed local, finite type iff f.g. stalk, Galois trivialization and the componentwise test all checked. R : Type (u+1) is the project convention and matches the landed consumers. Edge cases R=0, empty scheme, empty diagrams, infinite modules OK. Only the item theorem is sorry; docstrings and verbatim statements OK. The Proetale import is needed for the Subcanonical instance (tested by dropping it), not a pro-etale substitute. nt_compile --json clean: 5.3 s and 31.3 s, rc 0.
